s13-introduction-to-trees.trick: A binary tree is made of nodes with at most two children. A root pointer identifies the tree, and nullptr represents an absent child.
s13-introduction-to-trees.space: O(h) call stack, h = tree height

s13-binary-tree-representation-in-c.trick: Represent each C++ node with a value and two child pointers. Connect nodes through those pointers; the root is the entry point.

s13-binary-tree-representation-in-java.trick: This roadmap lesson uses a Java Node class; the equivalent C++ representation is a node class with references expressed as pointers.

s13-binary-tree-traversals-in-binary-tre.trick: The three depth-first orders differ only in when the root is recorded: before left (preorder), between children (inorder), or after right (postorder).

s13-preorder-traversal-of-binary-tree.trick: Visit root, then left subtree, then right subtree.

s13-inorder-traversal-of-binary-tree.trick: Visit left subtree, root, then right subtree.

s13-post-order-traversal-of-binary-tree.trick: Visit left subtree, right subtree, then root.

s13-level-order-traversal-level-order-tr.trick: Use a queue to process each level. Copy a level normally for BFS order and reverse alternate levels for the spiral form.

s13-iterative-preorder-traversal-of-bina.trick: A stack replaces recursion. Push right before left so the left child is processed first.

s13-iterative-inorder-traversal-of-binar.trick: Keep pushing left children. On reaching nullptr, pop the next node to visit and continue into its right subtree.

s13-post-order-traversal-of-binary-tree-.trick: The first stack visits root, right, left. The second stack reverses that order into left, right, root.
Keep ancestors on one stack. A node can be emitted only after its right subtree has been visited or if it has no right child.

s13-preorder-inorder-and-postorder-trave.trick: Give each stack frame a phase: 1 records preorder, 2 records inorder, and 3 records postorder. Push child frames between phases.

s13-height-of-a-binary-tree.trick: The height of an empty tree is zero; otherwise it is one plus the taller child height.

s13-check-if-the-binary-tree-is-height-b.trick: Compute subtree heights bottom-up. Return -1 immediately when one child is unbalanced or their heights differ by more than one.

s13-diameter-of-binary-tree.trick: At each node, a path through it has leftHeight + rightHeight edges. Compute heights once while updating the largest such path.

s13-maximum-path-sum.trick: A path through a node can take positive gains from both children. Return only the better one-sided gain to its parent.

s13-check-if-two-trees-are-identical-or-.trick: Two trees match only when both roots are absent or their values and corresponding left and right subtrees match.

s13-zig-zag-traversal-of-binary-tree.trick: Run level-order BFS. Write each level into normal or reversed positions depending on its direction.

s13-boundary-traversal-of-binary-tree.trick: Collect root, non-leaf left boundary, leaves from left to right, and non-leaf right boundary in reverse order.

s13-vertical-order-traversal-of-binary-t.trick: Record each node by column and row. At equal column and row, order values ascending with a multiset.

s13-top-view-of-binary-tree.trick: BFS visits shallower nodes first. Keep only the first node seen in each horizontal column, then read columns left to right.

s13-bottom-view-of-binary-tree.trick: BFS through nodes while overwriting the value at each horizontal column. Later (deeper or equally deep) nodes remain visible.

s13-right-left-view-of-binary-tree.trick: In each BFS level, the first node is visible from the left and the last from the right.

s13-symmetric-binary-tree.trick: Compare the left subtree against the right as mirrors: outer children match and inner children match.

s13-root-to-node-path-in-binary-tree.trick: DFS records the current node before descending. If neither child contains the target, remove this node while backtracking.

s13-lca-in-binary-tree.trick: A node is the lowest common ancestor if p and q are found in different child subtrees, or if the node itself equals one target.

s13-maximum-width-of-a-binary-tree.trick: Index each level as in a complete binary tree, but subtract the first index of every level to keep numbers small. Width includes gaps between endpoints.

s13-check-for-children-sum-property.trick: Every non-leaf node must equal the sum of its existing children's values. A leaf satisfies the property automatically.

s13-print-all-the-nodes-at-a-distance-of.trick: Record parent links with BFS, then BFS outward from the target through left, right, and parent links for exactly k edges.

s13-minimum-time-taken-to-burn-the-binar.trick: Build parent links, then spread fire from the target one BFS layer per unit of time through children and parent.

s13-count-total-nodes-in-a-complete-bina.trick: If the leftmost and rightmost heights match, the subtree is perfect and has 2^height−1 nodes. Otherwise recurse into both children.
s13-count-total-nodes-in-a-complete-bina.time: O(log² n) for a complete tree

s13-requirements-needed-to-construct-a-u.trick: With distinct node values, inorder plus preorder or inorder plus postorder fixes a unique binary tree. Preorder plus postorder alone usually does not.

s13-construct-binary-tree-from-inorder-a.trick: Preorder supplies each subtree's root. Its index in inorder divides that subtree into left and right ranges.
s13-construct-binary-tree-from-inorder-a.space: O(n) index map and call stack

s13-construct-the-binary-tree-from-posto.trick: Read postorder backwards to get each root. Split its inorder range and build the right subtree before the left.
s13-construct-the-binary-tree-from-posto.space: O(n) index map and call stack

s13-serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tre.trick: BFS writes each node value and '#' for missing children. Read the same tokens in BFS order to reconstruct exact child positions.

s13-morris-preorder-traversal-of-a-binar.trick: Temporarily thread each left subtree's rightmost node back to its parent. Visit a node on first arrival and restore its thread on second arrival.

s13-morris-inorder-traversal-of-a-binary.trick: Thread each left subtree's rightmost node to its parent. Visit the parent only after returning through that thread, then restore the link.

s13-flatten-binary-tree-to-linkedlist.trick: At each node with a left child, move its left subtree to the right and attach the old right subtree after that left subtree's rightmost node.
